price_note: OpenRice range HK$51–100 per person; Michelin lists it as $
intro: A no-frills neighbourhood Cantonese spot famous for claypot rice cooked to order over the flame, with a crispy scorched rice crust at the bottom. Listed in the Michelin Guide Hong Kong.
must_order: Eel & chicken claypot rice (白鱔滑雞煲仔飯)
Beef with egg claypot rice (窩蛋牛肉煲仔飯)
Salt & pepper Bombay duck (椒鹽九肚魚)
reviews: Reviewers rave about the claypot rice and its crust, and it is consistently tipped as worth queueing for; common complaints are long evening queues (some bloggers report up to two hours), basic surroundings and cash only.
group_friendly: Takes phone reservations (Michelin: manages its own bookings) – book ahead for a group and order the claypot rice first since it takes time. Expect a queue without a booking.
hours_note: Claypot rice is dinner only; Michelin lists 5pm–10pm daily (older sources list a lunch session too).
address: Shop 1, G/F, Wo Yick Mansion, 263 Queen's Road West, Sai Ying Pun (西營盤皇后大道西263號和益大廈地下1號舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

cuisine: Hong Kong-style chicken hotpot (cooked food centre)
price_note: OpenRice range HK$101–200 per person; one blog notes a chicken pot (~HK$168, 2016) feeds about three
intro: A stall in the Smithfield municipal cooked food centre (a government-run hawker hall above the wet market) serving spicy Hong Kong-style chicken pot – a sizzling pot of chicken in a spiced sauce that, once eaten, is topped up with broth to become hotpot. The OpenRice listing name is simply '雞煲' (Chicken Pot); no other stall name could be confirmed.
must_order: Dai Tat Dei chicken pot (大笪地雞煲)
Beer flambé chicken pot (啤酒火焰雞煲)
Sweet potato glass noodles for the hotpot (紅薯粉)
reviews: Reviews are mostly positive: tender chicken, a fun beer-flambé at the table and friendly staff; some found the chicken tough or the beef served half-frozen. Plastic stools, shared hall atmosphere.
group_friendly: Very group-friendly in the cooked-food-centre style (big round tables), but no online booking shown – call ahead. Cash/AlipayHK only per OpenRice.
hours_note: OpenRice: 5pm–11pm, closed Wednesdays, last order 9:30pm (a video lists 5pm–10:30pm).
address: Cooked Food Centre, 2/F, Smithfield Municipal Services Building, 12K Smithfield, Kennedy Town (堅尼地城士美菲路12K號士美菲路市政大廈2樓熟食中心)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: OpenRice range HK$101–200; reviews cite ~HK$150 per person
intro: A colourful, Thai-chef-run restaurant serving punchy, authentically spicy Thai dishes; staff ask how hot you want things.
must_order: Salted egg yolk squid (鹹蛋魷魚)
Thai fried rice noodles (泰式炒金邊粉)
reviews: Highly rated on OpenRice (very few negative reviews); diners praise authentic flavours, salted-egg dishes and friendly service. Expect real chilli heat; 10% service charge.
group_friendly: Online reservation available via OpenRice; has a bar counter and long tables. Booking recommended for groups.
address: G/F, 390A Des Voeux Road West, Shek Tong Tsui (石塘咀德輔道西390A號地舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: Reviews cite cheese kimchi pancake HK$138, pork belly BBQ HK$220, bossam set HK$240 (sharing dishes); roughly HK$200–300 per person
intro: A bright green-and-white Korean restaurant run by Korean staff, serving home-style sharing plates, banchan and a wide makgeolli (rice wine) list.
reviews: Reviewers praise generous portions, good banchan, tender bossam and cold buckwheat noodles at fair prices; it gets fully booked, even on rainy days.
group_friendly: Spacious open-plan room; online booking via OpenRice and Bistrochat – book ahead for groups. Pet-friendly.
address: G/F, 46C High Street, Sai Ying Pun (西營盤高街46C號地舖)
coord_note: approx (geocoded to 46 High Street next door)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: Ramen ~HK$88–118 per bowl per reviews
intro: A newer, viral ramen shop specialising in chicken broths – both a clear chicken-clam broth and a rich creamy chicken paitan.
must_order: Clear chicken broth & clam ramen (雞清湯貝汁蜆拉麵)
Rich chicken paitan truffle ramen (濃厚雞白湯松露拉麵)
reviews: Opinion is split: some love the thick, creamy broth, others find it less rich than the hype or the noodles too soft. Queues are long – reports of ~1 to 1.5 hours.
group_friendly: Small ramen shop with a long queue; not suited to large groups – go in twos or threes, off-peak.
address: Shop E, G/F, Full Harvest Building, 6-18 Hau Wo Street, Kennedy Town (堅尼地城厚和街6-18號滿發大廈地下E號舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: unknown overall range; individual items in reviews run ~HK$10 (zucchini) to HK$88 (garlic razor clams), fried pigeon HK$58; 10% service charge
intro: A neon-signed, izakaya-style grill bar (formerly 'BBQ') doing made-to-order skewers and Hong Kong snacks with beer – a fun, casual night out.
must_order: Grilled garlic razor clams (蒜蓉燒蟶子)
reviews: Reviewers praise well-grilled skewers (chicken skin 'crispier than chips') at fair prices and cheap beer deals; a few note some items are small or bony.
group_friendly: Reviewers say to book in advance; call for group tables.
hours_note: unknown (promoted as a late-night spot on Instagram)
address: G/F, 129 Third Street, Sai Ying Pun (西營盤第三街129號地舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: exact range unknown; reviews say prices are not expensive
intro: A cat-themed dessert café (part of a small local chain) serving traditional Chinese sweet soups alongside waffles and savoury snacks.
must_order: Coconut steamed milk with egg white (椰皇燉鮮奶蛋白)
White peach yakult slush (白桃乳酸沙冰)
reviews: Reviews are positive about smooth sesame soup and almond tea, generous portions and good value; the cat décor is a draw.
group_friendly: unknown – small café; fine for small groups.
address: Shop E, G/F, Smithfield Walk / Luen Fat Apartments, 45-51 Smithfield, Kennedy Town (堅尼地城士美菲路45-51號 地下E號舖; also listed as 士美菲路49號聯發新樓地下E舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: Set lunches ~HK$200 per person (2026 reviews); dinner omakase price unknown (a 2016 review paid ~HK$1,060)
intro: A long-running neighbourhood Japanese restaurant known for good-value lunch sets (donburi, grilled steak, sushi) and chef's-choice omakase at dinner.
must_order: Scallop, salmon & sea urchin donburi set (帆立貝三文魚海膽丼定食)
Grilled steak set (網燒牛扒定食)
reviews: Recent reviews like the generous lunch sets (starter, salad, miso soup, main, dessert) and long track record; an older review found dinner omakase good but only average value.
group_friendly: unknown – call to book.
address: Shop 5, G/F, Grand Fortune Mansion, 1 Davis Street, Kennedy Town (堅尼地城爹核士街1號裕福大廈地下5號舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: exact range unknown; reviews call it cheap
intro: A cult old-school dim sum house that opens at 3am, serving night owls, taxi drivers and early risers with classic dim sum, some still on trolleys.
must_order: Salted egg custard lava buns (流沙包)
reviews: Loved for authentic, cheap dim sum and atmosphere; complaints are long queues at peak times, no proper queue system (you hunt for seats and share tables), no English menu and limited English. Bring cash (payment reports conflict; OpenRice lists Octopus/Alipay too).
group_friendly: Not bookable; small groups only and expect shared tables. Best for a 3–6am post-drinks visit or early morning.
address: Shop C, G/F, 8 Smithfield, Kennedy Town (堅尼地城士美菲路8號地下C號舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: ~HK$100 per person per a 2024 review
intro: A bright, clean Sichuan-style skewer shop: grilled meat, seafood and veg skewers with numbing-spicy seasoning, kept warm over a candle at the table.
reviews: Diners like the variety and adjustable spice (non-spicy cumin or hot chilli rub); delivery reviewers complain skewers are small.
group_friendly: unknown – call ahead for groups.
address: Shop 6, G/F, Fung Yu Building, 182-190 Third Street, Shek Tong Tsui (石塘咀第三街182-190號豐裕大廈地下6號舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: Braised pork rice ~HK$42–46; meals roughly under HK$100
intro: A small, popular Taiwanese eatery (with branches elsewhere in HK) known for braised pork rice and oyster vermicelli; listed in the Michelin Guide Hong Kong.
must_order: Oyster & intestine vermicelli (蚵仔大腸麵線)
Chicken rice with egg (爆蛋雞肉飯)
Pork floss cheese egg crepe (肉鬆起司蛋餅)
reviews: Diners praise the braised pork rice and value; some say portions are small. Queues at peak times – reports of 20–45 minutes at dinner.
group_friendly: Small shop with queues; not ideal for big groups – split up or go off-peak.
hours_note: Sources conflict: 11am–10pm closed Monday (Time Out) vs 11am–9pm closed Tuesday (review) – check.
address: G/F, 31 North Street, Kennedy Town (堅尼地城北街31號地舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: OpenRice range HK$201–400 per person; 10% service charge
intro: The Kennedy Town branch of a popular Hong Kong fresh-pasta chain, with big open windows onto the street and pasta made daily.
must_order: Orecchiette with spicy sausage (辣肉腸貓耳朵粉)
Pappardelle with beef cheek or lamb ragù (寬條麵)
reviews: Generally well rated on OpenRice; fans like the fresh pasta, burrata and tiramisu, while some find portions small or the food inconsistent.
group_friendly: Online booking on OpenRice/Pici site; good for medium groups – book ahead. Outdoor seating.
address: G/F, Hang Yu Building, 45-55 Cadogan Street, Kennedy Town (堅尼地城加多近街45-55號恆裕大廈地舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: From ~HK$40 per bowl (2022 report)
intro: A Taiwanese dessert shop making chewy taro, sweet potato and purple yam balls by hand daily, served with grass jelly, mango or shaved ice.
must_order: Traditional grass jelly with taro balls (傳統仙草芋圓)
Taro grass jelly with taro balls (芋香仙草芋圓)
Irwin mango sago with taro balls (愛文芒甘露芋圓)
Mango milk snow ice (芒果牛奶棉花冰)
reviews: Reviewers like the generous, chewy handmade taro balls and mango desserts; there is upstairs booth seating.
group_friendly: unknown – small dessert shop; fine for small groups.
address: G/F, 27 Water Street, Sai Ying Pun (西營盤水街27號地舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

cuisine: Dim sum & cha chaan teng (HK café)
price_note: OpenRice range HK$51–100 per person
intro: A casual dim sum and cha chaan teng (Hong Kong diner) famous for creative twists like oozing 'lava' French toast and extra-thick sesame shrimp toast.
must_order: Salted egg yolk lava French toast (流沙西多士)
Prawn roll with ginger & century egg (子薑皮蛋蝦卷)
reviews: Popular with locals and visitors for its Instagrammable toasts; some find the lava filling watery or flavours inconsistent.
group_friendly: unknown – casual seating; Klook sells priority-pass sets, suggesting queues at peak times.
hours_note: Reported 8am–6pm, closed Monday (Yelp, Dec 2025) – other sources differ; check.
address: Shop H1, G/F, Tung Lee Mansion, 1C-1K Water Street, Sai Ying Pun (西營盤水街1C-1K號東利大廈地下H1號舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: unknown
intro: A tiny ramen shop tucked in a side lane, run by a Hokkaido-born Japanese chef who makes his own noodles; best known for tsukemen (noodles dipped into a thick broth).
must_order: Black garlic oil tsukemen (黑蒜油湯沾麵)
Shrimp miso tsukemen (蝦味噌湯沾麵)
Tonkotsu chashu tsukemen (豚骨湯叉燒沾麵)
reviews: Noodles are widely praised, but some reviewers find the broth too salty/MSG-heavy or the dipping sauce too thin; service reviews are mixed. Cash payment noted.
group_friendly: Only ~20 seats; queues at noon – small groups only.
hours_note: Lunch 11:30am–3pm and dinner 6pm–9pm, closed Sunday (sources vary).
address: G/F, Kam Ling Court, 16 Whitty Street, Shek Tong Tsui (石塘咀屈地街16號金陵大廈地舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: A lunch set was reported at HK$158 (older review); exact current range unknown
intro: A Malaysian/Singaporean hawker-style restaurant on Level 2 of JEN Hong Kong by Shangri-La, a 2-minute walk from HKU MTR, cooking dishes from Penang, Ipoh and Kuala Lumpur. It received a Michelin 'recommended' mention in 2014–2015.
reviews: Reviews are mixed but generally positive: nasi lemak rice, sambal and crispy anchovies are praised; laksa ranges from 'close to authentic' to 'average'. Most reviews online are older.
group_friendly: Hotel restaurant – easiest place on this list for a large group; book online (inline) or by phone.
address: 2/F, JEN Hong Kong by Shangri-La, 508 Queen's Road West, Shek Tong Tsui (石塘咀皇后大道西508號香港JEN酒店2樓)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: OpenRice range HK$51–100; add-on snacks HK$16–28
intro: The new (May 2026) Kennedy Town branch of a Yuen Long cart-noodle brand founded in 1962: pick your noodles, broth and toppings from a long list – a classic Hong Kong street-food format, here with retro décor and booths.
must_order: Cart noodles with your choice of toppings (自選車仔麵)
Crispy shrimp-paste siu mai (熟蝦醬脆燒賣)
Deep-fried whole-prawn wontons (炸原隻鮮蝦雲吞)
reviews: Too new for many reviews of this branch; the chain is generally liked for affordable, customisable cart noodles.
group_friendly: Lots of booth seating per HK01 – fine for small-to-medium groups; no booking info.
address: Shop 6, G/F, Imperial Kennedy, 68 Belcher's Street, Kennedy Town (堅尼地城卑路乍街68號Imperial Kennedy地下6號舖; HK01 gives No. 80)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

name_en: A One Pork Chop Spicy Rice Noodles
price_note: Under ~HK$50; pork chop noodles ~HK$41–44
intro: A local favourite for sour-and-spicy rice noodle soup topped with a fried, overnight-marinated pork chop; you choose your spice level.
must_order: Pork chop sour & spicy rice noodles (豬扒酸辣米綫)
Pork chop on its own (單點豬扒)
reviews: Reviewers praise the fresh-fried, well-marinated pork chop and chewy thick noodles; this branch is often called better than other branches. Can have queues.
group_friendly: Small, quick noodle shop – fine for small groups, not for bookings.
address: Shop C1, G/F, Hoi To Court, 7-11 Belcher's Street, Kennedy Town (堅尼地城卑路乍街7-11號海都樓地下C1號舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

cuisine: Spanish gin & tonic bar with tapas
price_note: G&Ts ~HK$120–160 (premium up to ~HK$240); minimum spend for reservations after 7:30pm
intro: A hidden basement bar in a former ping-pong hall behind a pink door – Spanish-style gin & tonics, tapas, and rotating Hong Kong art exhibitions.
must_order: Spanish-style gin & tonic (西班牙式金湯力)
reviews: Reviewers love the cavernous space and the 40+ gin selection with careful tonic pairing; complaints are high prices, uneven service and ordinary tapas. Entrance easy to miss.
group_friendly: Takes table and event reservations (email info@pingpong129.com or phone); group minimum spend after 7:30pm. Big space – good for a class gathering.
address: L/G, Nam Cheong House, 129-135 Second Street, Sai Ying Pun (西營盤第二街129-135號南昌樓地舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: Under ~HK$50 per person (feehk, 2022)
intro: A branch of one of Hong Kong's best-known noodle chains: build your own bowl of rice noodles in sour-spicy or mala broth, choosing toppings and spice level.
must_order: Sour & spicy rice noodles with your choice of toppings (酸辣米線)
reviews: A dependable, cheap chain staple; few branch-specific reviews (about 19 on OpenRice).
group_friendly: Fast-casual; fine for small groups, no booking needed.
address: Shop 8, G/F, Imperial Kennedy, 68 Belcher's Street, Kennedy Town (堅尼地城卑路乍街68號Imperial Kennedy地下8號舖)
coord_note: building-level; same building as Wing Nin Noodle
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: Under ~HK$50 per person; mango desserts ~HK$38–48
intro: A neighbourhood sweet-soup shop (moved here from Water Street) serving traditional Chinese desserts and newer mango creations until late.
must_order: Mango with glutinous balls (多芒丸圓)
reviews: Mixed: fans like the generous, cheap mango desserts and smooth tofu pudding; others find quality inconsistent (Tripadvisor 3.0/5).
group_friendly: About 20 seats – OK for small groups.
hours_note: 2pm–1am daily; dine-in may stop at midnight with takeaway till 1am.
address: G/F, 208 Des Voeux Road West, Sai Ying Pun (西營盤德輔道西208號地舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: unknown; happy hour 4pm–7pm
intro: A long-running, casual Mexican bar-restaurant with a big tequila list, plus an upstairs room ('Tequila Upstairs') for private parties.
must_order: Frozen or jalapeño margarita (瑪格麗特)
reviews: Tripadvisor 4.3/5 – generous portions and consistent food; margaritas divide opinion (some too sweet/artificial); can be dark inside; book at weekends.
group_friendly: Good for groups – upstairs private-party space; book ahead for weekends.
address: G/F, 1 Davis Street, Kennedy Town (堅尼地城爹核士街1號地舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: Roughly under HK$50 per person (estimate on feehk); cash/FPS
intro: An old-school late-night dessert-and-snack shop open into the small hours, known for its 'five-colour' cold noodles alongside sweet soups.
reviews: unknown – few recent reviews found (latest OpenRice review seen March 2025).
group_friendly: unknown
hours_note: 6pm–3am, closed Saturday (OpenRice/Facebook); another listing says 5pm–2am daily.
address: G/F, Sun Fat Building, 12S-12T Smithfield, Kennedy Town (堅尼地城士美菲路12S-12T號新發大廈地舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: unknown; ticketed live shows listed on its website
intro: A Japanese-style 'jazz kissa' – a listening café by day and jazz bar by night, playing vinyl on a high-end sound system, with weekly live sets by local and international musicians. Run by musicians.
reviews: Reviewers love the music-first atmosphere, record collection and album requests; it's a quiet listening space rather than a party bar.
group_friendly: Listening-focused room – better for small groups; check the website for ticketed live shows.
address: G/F, 106-112 First Street, Sai Ying Pun (西營盤第一街112號地舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

cuisine: Natural / small-batch wine bar with small plates
price_note: 2024: wines ~HK$120–150/glass, flights HK$180 (3) / HK$280 (5); plates ~HK$55–138
intro: A wine bar and bottle shop focused on small-batch, sustainable and natural wines, with a casual ground-floor bar and an upstairs room for sharing plates of French-American comfort food.
must_order: Aubergine with whipped roast chilli (茄子配烤辣椒醬)
reviews: Reviewers call it one of the most interesting wine bars in town with knowledgeable staff; complaints are a small bar counter, loud music and acoustics that make conversation hard.
group_friendly: Upstairs dining room and weekly events; book ahead for groups.
hours_note: Mon–Fri 4pm–11pm, Sat–Sun 12pm–11pm (official site); Star Wine List shows closed Mondays.
address: Shop A, G/F, 6-8 Second Street, Sai Ying Pun (西營盤第二街6-8號地下A號舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: OpenRice range HK$101–200; cocktails ~HK$130; 10% service charge
intro: A cosy cocktail bar with a wall of vinyl records where guests can pick and play albums; inventive cocktails using tea and local flavours. [Resolved from Google Maps link maps.app.goo.gl/9DruodWWAmWK5vA99]
must_order: Pricky Lychee – gin, elderflower, lychee, Sichuan pepper
reviews: Reviewers like the stylish, cosy space, the record wall and staff recommendations; some note it is small and not every drink lands.
group_friendly: Small space – best for small groups.
address: G/F, 61 High Street, Sai Ying Pun (西營盤高街61號地舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: unknown
intro: A small hidden bar off Water Street pairing Chinese teas with spirits, led by a mixologist who says he previously worked at a Michelin two-star restaurant. [Resolved from Google Maps link maps.app.goo.gl/URmsAjJC1piUYSYc8]
reviews: Very few reviews online yet; one Tripadvisor reviewer called the tea cocktails delicious.
group_friendly: unknown – likely small; contact via Threads/Instagram @dontail.bar.
address: Shop D, G/F, Sam To Lane, 4 Water Street, Sai Ying Pun (西營盤水街4號三多里地下D舖)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)

price_note: Wines sold at retail price to drink in or take away; croque raclette ~HK$100
intro: A tiny French wine shop-cum-bar (self-styled 'grumpiest wine pub') where you drink French bottles at retail prices with cheese, cold cuts and oysters. [Resolved from Google Maps link maps.app.goo.gl/pMTv9GjtLzrKx4Qv7]
must_order: Cheese & charcuterie board (芝士凍肉拼盤)
reviews: Highly rated (Restaurant Guru 4.8/5 from 138 reviews); people praise reasonable prices, cheese and oysters. Seats only about a dozen inside, with some outdoor seating.
group_friendly: Seats ~12 inside – small groups only; phone reservations listed on OpenRice.
address: Shop E, G/F, Fook Moon Building, 56-72 Third Street, Sai Ying Pun (西營盤第三街56-72號福滿大廈地下E號舖)

price_note: 'Chaos Menu' ~HK$598 (5 courses) / HK$728 (7 courses) per Time Out Sept 2026 (other listings HK$628–758); drinks pairing extra (~HK$258)
intro: A terracotta-toned chef's-table restaurant run by Malaysian-Australian chef Gavin Chin, whose omakase-style 'Chaos Menu' uses local wet-market produce with Malay, Chinese and Australian flavours. [Resolved from Google Maps link maps.app.goo.gl/RgKN9LuYtrYZNgUv9]
must_order: 14-hour beef short rib rendang (14小時仁當牛肋骨)
reviews: OpenRice diners are largely enthusiastic about the inventive dishes; critics say the concept feels unfocused and service uneven (Tripadvisor 3.0/5 from few reviews).
group_friendly: Tasting-menu format – book ahead; call/WhatsApp to arrange a group.
address: Shop B, G/F, Kenbo Commercial Building, 335-339 Queen's Road West, Sai Ying Pun (西營盤皇后大道西335-339號)
sources: https://www.als.gov.hk (HK Gov Address Lookup Service, building-level geocode)
